item.text:
## 2B.9 Research Note: Vladimir Putin, Russia, 2023

**Working judgment:** **Mostly no.** I found repeated denial and deflection, not accountability. The strongest 2023 evidence shows Putin rejecting war-crime allegations, blaming Ukraine/West for major civilian-harm events, and continuing to justify the war in defensive terms despite later evidence and internal contradiction.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** `Press Briefing on Crimes Against Humanity Designation by Dr. Beth Van Schaack`  
  **Publisher:** U.S. Department of State  
  **Date:** 22 Feb 2023  
  **URL:** [https://2021-2025.state.gov/press-briefing-on-crimes-against-humanity-designation-by-dr-beth-van-schaack-ambassador-at-large-for-global-criminal-justice/](https://2021-2025.state.gov/press-briefing-on-crimes-against-humanity-designation-by-dr-beth-van-schaack-ambassador-at-large-for-global-criminal-justice/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** The State Department said it had determined members of Russia’s forces and other Russian officials committed crimes against humanity, including execution-style killings, torture, rape, and deportation of civilians and children. This is strong evidence of illegal conduct that Putin did not publicly accept responsibility for.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.2`

- **Title:** `Putin repeats assertion that Russia did not start war in Ukraine`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** 10 May 2023  
  **URL:** [https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-repeats-assertion-that-russia-did-not-start-war-in-ukraine-3180367](https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-repeats-assertion-that-russia-did-not-start-war-in-ukraine-3180367)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin reiterated that Russia did not start the war and cast it as a necessary special military operation to stop threats from Ukraine and the West. This is direct denial rather than accountability, and it stayed in place even as contrary evidence accumulated.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.9`, `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.1`

- **Title:** `Putin accuses Ukraine of destroying the Kakhovka dam at behest of West`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 7 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://theprint.in/world/putin-accuses-ukraine-of-destroying-the-kakhovka-dam-at-behest-of-west/1617195/](https://theprint.in/world/putin-accuses-ukraine-of-destroying-the-kakhovka-dam-at-behest-of-west/1617195/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** After the Kakhovka dam breach, Putin accused Ukraine of a “barbaric” war crime and said Kyiv had acted at the suggestion of Western sponsors, while ordering rescue efforts in the area. This is a clear example of blame-shifting: a limited operational response without acceptance of responsibility or evidence-backed self-criticism.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.6`

- **Title:** `TIMELINE: Putin's key moments in Ukraine as war enters 4th year`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters Connect  
  **Date:** 24 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/timeline-putins-key-moments-in-ukraine-as-war-enters-4th-year/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjM6bmV3c21sX1ZBMjUyMDI0MDYyMDIzUlAx](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/timeline-putins-key-moments-in-ukraine-as-war-enters-4th-year/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjM6bmV3c21sX1ZBMjUyMDI0MDYyMDIzUlAx)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Reuters notes that on April 12 Putin dismissed Ukrainian and Western claims that Russia had committed war crimes as fakes, while vowing Russian victory. This is a direct refusal to acknowledge civilian harm or legal wrongdoing.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.9`, `2B.6`, `2B.2`

- **Title:** `Wagner mercenary chief says Russia's war in Ukraine based on lies`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via MarketScreener  
  **Date:** 23 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/currency/US-DOLLAR-RUSSIAN-ROUBLE--2370597/news/Wagner-mercenary-chief-says-Russia-s-war-in-Ukraine-based-on-lies-44178406/](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/currency/US-DOLLAR-RUSSIAN-ROUBLE--2370597/news/Wagner-mercenary-chief-says-Russia-s-war-in-Ukraine-based-on-lies-44178406/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Prigozhin publicly said the Kremlin’s rationale for invading Ukraine was based on lies and that the military had misled Putin and society about the threat. This is not Putin’s accountability, but it is strong later evidence contradicting the stated justification for conflict.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.9`, `2B.6`, `2B.5`

- **Title:** `Russia - Ukraine international armed conflict: ICRC continues to help people in need`  
  **Publisher:** ICRC  
  **Date:** 14 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.icrc.org/en/document/russia-ukraine-international-armed-conflict-icrc-continues-to-help-people-in-need](https://www.icrc.org/en/document/russia-ukraine-international-armed-conflict-icrc-continues-to-help-people-in-need)  
  **Claim-level summary:** The ICRC said increased military operations and the destruction of the Nova Kakhovka dam were creating additional threats to civilians. This confirms the scale of harm underlying the accountability question, but it also shows no sign of Putin publicly owning that harm or changing course because of it.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.9`, `2B.4`

### Search gap

I did **not** find credible 2023 evidence that Putin accepted responsibility for military failures, civilian harm, illegal conduct, or later evidence contradicting the war’s justification. The pattern is denial, blame-shifting, and insistence on the original justification.

### Bottom line

**Mostly no.** Putin did not publicly accept accountability in 2023; he denied war-crime claims, blamed Ukraine and the West for civilian-harm events, and continued to defend the invasion even as contradictory evidence surfaced.
